reference.source: Standard breast surgery textbook and breast pathology guidance
clinicalPearls: Sclerosing adenosis is a benign proliferative lesion of the terminal duct lobular unit that is a recognised mimic of malignancy clinically, radiologically, and histologically
It is frequently an incidental microscopic finding but can form a palpable lump or produce a mammographic abnormality, often clustered microcalcification
It falls within the spectrum of fibrocystic and proliferative breast change and may coexist with other benign lesions such as radial scars and papillomas
The distorted proliferation of glands within fibrous stroma can imitate invasive carcinoma on imaging and on core biopsy, making expert pathological interpretation essential
Triple assessment with core biopsy is used to distinguish it from cancer, and immunohistochemistry demonstrating an intact myoepithelial layer helps confirm its benign nature
When the lesion causes suspicious calcification or a mass, or when biopsy shows associated atypia, diagnostic excision may be required
Uncomplicated sclerosing adenosis needs no treatment beyond reassurance once malignancy is excluded
It is associated with a small increase in future breast cancer risk, greater when accompanied by atypical hyperplasia
reference.pathophysiology: Sclerosing adenosis is characterised by an increase in the number of acini within the lobule (adenosis) accompanied by proliferation of fibrous stroma that compresses and distorts the proliferating glands. This combination of glandular proliferation and stromal sclerosis produces a swirling, infiltrative-looking architecture that can closely resemble invasive carcinoma, and dystrophic calcification within the lesion often generates suspicious microcalcification on mammography. The key feature confirming benignity is preservation of the outer myoepithelial cell layer around the distorted glands, which is retained in adenosis but lost in invasive cancer, and which can be highlighted with immunohistochemical markers.
additionalDifferentials: Radial scar or complex sclerosing lesion
additionalInvestigations: Clinical examination as part of triple assessment when a lump is present
Mammography, which may reveal clustered microcalcification or a distortion
Core needle biopsy with expert histological review
Immunohistochemistry for myoepithelial markers to confirm an intact myoepithelial layer
Diagnostic excision where imaging is suspicious or atypia is found on biopsy
redFlags: Suspicious microcalcification or architectural distortion on imaging
Histological features overlapping with tubular carcinoma or associated atypia
A discrete or enlarging palpable mass
Coexisting atypical hyperplasia, which raises future cancer risk
reference.prognosis: Sclerosing adenosis is benign with a good prognosis once malignancy is excluded, requiring no treatment in most cases, though it confers a modest increase in future breast cancer risk that is greater if atypical hyperplasia is also present.
pitfalls: Overcalling the lesion as invasive carcinoma on imaging or biopsy owing to its infiltrative appearance
Failing to use myoepithelial markers to distinguish it from cancer
Missing coexisting atypia or malignancy in an adjacent radial scar or papilloma
Ignoring discordance between suspicious imaging and a benign biopsy
Underestimating the associated future cancer risk when atypia is present
references: Standard breast pathology reference text on proliferative breast disease
Breast surgery guidance on benign proliferative lesions
management: Confirm benignity through triple assessment with core biopsy and myoepithelial immunohistochemistry, then reassure, as the lesion itself needs no treatment
Undertake diagnostic excision, for example vacuum-assisted or surgical, where imaging is suspicious, findings are discordant, or biopsy shows associated atypia
Manage coexisting proliferative lesions such as radial scars or papillomas on their own merits
Counsel on the modest increase in future breast-cancer risk, which is greater when atypical hyperplasia coexists
Enrol in appropriate mammographic surveillance according to individualised risk
Refer to a breast unit for expert pathological review given its close mimicry of carcinoma
